heading.en: Follow the spending, follow the earning

hook.en: Every rupee spent on a final good is a rupee earned by someone as wages, rent, interest or profit. So we can measure GDP by adding up either spending or earning.
hook.kn: ಅಂತಿಮ ಸರಕಿನ ಮೇಲೆ ವೆಚ್ಚವಾದ ಪ್ರತಿ ರೂಪಾಯಿಯೂ ಯಾರಿಗೋ ಕೂಲಿ, ಗೇಣಿ, ಬಡ್ಡಿ ಅಥವಾ ಲಾಭವಾಗಿ ಗಳಿಕೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ವೆಚ್ಚ ಅಥವಾ ಗಳಿಕೆ ಕೂಡಿಸಿ GDP ಅಳೆಯಬಹುದು.

title.en: Calculate GDP by the expenditure method
Calculate GDP by the income method

say.en: Every rupee spent on a final good is a rupee earned by someone as wages, rent, interest or profit. So we can measure GDP by adding up either spending or earning. In this lesson: Calculate GDP by the expenditure method.
Calculate GDP by the income method.
Exclude transfer payments correctly.

body.en: GDP is the sum of final *expenditure* on goods and services produced in the domestic economy: private final consumption expenditure (C), investment expenditure (I), government final consumption expenditure (G) and net exports (X − M). Imports are subtracted because they are produced abroad.
body.kn: GDP = ಖಾಸಗಿ ಅಂತಿಮ ಉಪಭೋಗ ವೆಚ್ಚ (C) + ಹೂಡಿಕೆ ವೆಚ್ಚ (I) + ಸರ್ಕಾರದ ಅಂತಿಮ ಉಪಭೋಗ ವೆಚ್ಚ (G) + ನಿವ್ವಳ ರಫ್ತು (X − M). ಆಮದುಗಳು ವಿದೇಶದಲ್ಲಿ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆಯಾದ್ದರಿಂದ ಕಳೆಯಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: On the board: Spending side and income side

say.en: By expenditure, GDP adds consumption, investment, government purchases and net exports.
With C 800, I 200, G 150, X 100 and M 120, GDP is 1,130 crore.
By income, GDP adds wages, rent, interest and profit: 1,000 crore.
Old-age pensions are transfer payments. No service is given in return, so leave them out.

body.en: GDP is also the sum of factor payments made by firms: wages (compensation of employees), rent, interest and profit. Transfer payments such as pensions, scholarships and unemployment allowances are left out, because no productive service is given in return.
body.kn: GDP = ಉತ್ಪಾದನಾಂಗ ಪಾವತಿಗಳ ಮೊತ್ತ: ಕೂಲಿ (ನೌಕರರ ಪರಿಹಾರ), ಗೇಣಿ, ಬಡ್ಡಿ ಮತ್ತು ಲಾಭ. ಪಿಂಚಣಿ, ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿವೇತನದಂತಹ ವರ್ಗಾವಣೆ ಪಾವತಿಗಳನ್ನು ಸೇರಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ, ಏಕೆಂದರೆ ಅವುಗಳಿಗೆ ಪ್ರತಿಯಾಗಿ ಉತ್ಪಾದಕ ಸೇವೆ ಇಲ್ಲ.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. An economy has: private consumption ₹800 crore, investment ₹200 crore, government purchases ₹150 crore, exports ₹100 crore, imports ₹120 crore. Find GDP by the expenditure method.

say.en: Let us work through this together. An economy has: private consumption 800 rupees crore, investment 200 rupees crore, government purchases 150 rupees crore, exports 100 rupees crore, imports 120 rupees crore. Find GDP by the expenditure method.
Net exports equals 100 minus 120 equals minus 20 rupees crore.
GDP equals 800 plus 200 plus 150 plus minus 20.
GDP equals 1,130 rupees crore.
So the answer is GDP at market price equals 1,130 rupees crore.

say.en: Let us work through this together. The firms of an economy pay wages 600 rupees crore, rent 100 rupees crore, interest 80 rupees crore and earn profit 220 rupees crore. The government also pays old-age pensions of 40 rupees crore. Find GDP by the income method.
Factor incomes: 600 plus 100 plus 80 plus 220 equals 1,000 rupees crore.
Pensions are transfer payments: exclude them.
GDP income method equals 1,000 rupees crore.
So the answer is 1,000 rupees crore.

Competitive exam practice: CUET-pattern questions. Read every option before you choose. Which of the following are included in the national income of India?
A Wages paid to workers of a Mysuru factory
B Old-age pension paid by the government
C Purchase of a second-hand car
D Value of new machines produced during the year.
Wages are factor income and new machines are part of the year's output.
A pension is a transfer payment and a second-hand car was counted in the year it was made, so B and C are excluded.
